items.title: OpenAI shipped always-on agent infrastructure
items.oneliner: OpenAI turned ChatGPT into an agent platform with Dots, browser tools, plugins, and marketplace distribution.

items.title: OpenAI cut frontier model pricing hard
items.oneliner: GPT-6.1 Sol claims near-Astra performance at one-fifth the price, pushing cost pressure onto every model vendor.

items.title: OpenAI's revenue is nearing hyperscale
items.oneliner: OpenAI's reported $70B run rate means AI spend is no longer experimental budget; it is becoming core infrastructure.

items.title: OnePlus patched a root exploit chain
items.oneliner: An untrusted app could reach uid 0 on OnePlus phones, a reminder that Android attack chains still hide in OEM firmware.

items.title: PS5 exploitation now spans firmware 7.00-13.60
items.oneliner: The Relapse exploit covers PS5 firmware 7.00 through 13.60, showing consumer platforms remain fertile security research targets.

items.title: European data center transparency is failing
items.oneliner: Less than 25% of large Dutch data centers disclose water and power use, even as AI load keeps climbing.

items.title: McDonald's is testing AI-driven pricing suggestions
items.oneliner: McDonald's is using AI to suggest menu prices, which is where inference finally meets messy real-world margin optimization.

items.title: Rust compiler got materially faster again
items.oneliner: Rust cut mean compile wall time by 4.57% in two months, the kind of tooling gain developers feel every day.

items.title: Deser challenges Rust's serialization default
items.oneliner: Armin Ronacher's Deser rethinks Serde for huge untrusted JSON, trading format breadth for safer deep-nesting behavior.

items.title: NSL brings WSL-style isolation to Linux
items.oneliner: NSL packages signed distro containers for Linux developers, making disposable dev environments a first-class local workflow.
